title.zh: 卷三百二十八 列傳第二百十六 外國九 瓦剌 兀良哈
title.en: Volume 328 Biographies 216: Foreign States 9 - Oirats, Wuliangha
title.raw: 卷三百二十八 列傳第二百十六 外國九 瓦剌 兀良哈 Volume 328 Biographies 216: Foreign States 9 - Oirats, Wuliangha

sentences.zh: 瓦剌，蒙古部落也，在韃靼西。

translations.literal: The Oirats were a Mongol tribe, located to the west of the Tartars.
translations.idiomatic: The Oirats were a Mongol tribe situated west of the Tartars.

sentences.zh: 元亡，其強臣猛可帖木兒據之。

translations.literal: When the Yuan perished, its powerful minister Mokectemur seized control of them.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yuan fell, a powerful minister named Mokectemur took control of the tribe.

sentences.zh: 死，眾分為三，其渠曰馬哈木，曰太平，曰把禿孛羅。

translations.literal: He died; the masses split into three groups, their chieftains being Mahamu, Taiping, and Batu Boluo.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, the people divided into three factions, led by Mahamu, Taiping, and Batu Boluo.

sentences.zh: 成祖即位，遣使往告。

translations.literal: When the Chengzu Emperor took the throne, he sent envoys to announce it.
translations.idiomatic: Upon his accession, the Chengzu Emperor dispatched envoys to inform them.

sentences.zh: 永樂初，復數使鎮撫答哈帖木兒等諭之，並賜馬哈木等文綺有差。

translations.literal: In the early Yongle reign, he again repeatedly sent the pacification commissioner Dahar Temur and others to instruct them, and conferred varying grades of brocade on Mahamu and the others.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Yongle period, the emperor repeatedly sent pacification commissioners such as Dahar Temur to instruct them and granted Mahamu and his colleagues brocade in varying quantities.

sentences.zh: 六年冬，馬哈木等遣暖答失等隨亦剌思來朝貢馬，仍請封。

translations.literal: In the winter of the sixth year, Mahamu and others sent Nuandashi and others, accompanying Yilasi, to come to court and present horses as tribute, and again requested investiture.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the sixth year, Mahamu and his colleagues sent Nuandashi and others, accompanying Yilasi, to court with tribute horses and again petitioned for enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 明年夏，封馬哈木為特進金紫光祿大夫、順寧王；

translations.literal: The following summer, Mahamu was enfeoffed as Special Grand Master with the Golden Brilliant Ray Cap and Grand Seal, Shunningning King;
translations.idiomatic: The following summer, Mahamu was enfeoffed as Special Grand Master with the Golden Brilliant Ray Cap and Grand Seal and as King of Shunningning;

sentences.zh: 太平為特進金紫光祿大夫、賢義王；

translations.literal: Taiping as Special Grand Master with the Golden Brilliant Ray Cap and Grand Seal, Xianyi King;
translations.idiomatic: Taiping as Special Grand Master with the Golden Brilliant Ray Cap and Grand Seal and as King of Xianyi;

sentences.zh: 把禿孛羅為特進金紫光祿大夫、安樂王；

translations.literal: Batu Boluo as Special Grand Master with the Golden Brilliant Ray Cap and Grand Seal, Anle King;
translations.idiomatic: Batu Boluo as Special Grand Master with the Golden Brilliant Ray Cap and Grand Seal and as King of Anle;

sentences.zh: 賜印誥。

translations.literal: Seals and patent letters were conferred.
translations.idiomatic: They were granted seals and letters of patent.

sentences.zh: 暖答失等宴賚如例。

translations.literal: Nuandashi and the others were feasted and rewarded according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Nuandashi and his party were entertained and rewarded according to established practice.

sentences.zh: 八年春，瓦剌復貢馬謝恩。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eighth year, the Oirats again presented horses in tribute to express gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the eighth year, the Oirats again sent tribute horses to express their thanks.

sentences.zh: 自是歲一入貢。

translations.literal: From this time they paid tribute once a year.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter they sent tribute annually.

sentences.zh: 時元主本雅失裡偕其屬阿魯台居漠北，馬哈木乃以兵襲破之。

translations.literal: At that time the Yuan ruler Benyashili, together with his follower Arugtai, dwelt in the northern desert; Mahamu then attacked and defeated them with troops.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Yuan ruler Benyashili and his follower Arugtai were living in the northern steppe, and Mahamu attacked and routed them.

sentences.zh: 八年，帝既自將擊破本雅失裡及阿魯台兵，馬哈木上言請得早為滅寇計。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, after the emperor had personally led troops and defeated the armies of Benyashili and Arugtai, Mahamu submitted a memorial requesting permission to make early plans to destroy the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, after the emperor had personally led an expedition that broke the forces of Benyashili and Arugtai, Mahamu memorialized the throne asking to be allowed to plan early for their destruction.

sentences.zh: 十年，馬哈木遂攻殺本雅失裡。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Mahamu then attacked and killed Benyashili.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, Mahamu attacked and killed Benyashili.

sentences.zh: 復上言欲獻故元傳國璽，慮阿魯台來邀，請中國除之；

translations.literal: He again submitted a memorial stating his wish to present the former Yuan dynastic seal, but fearing Arugtai would come to intercept it, he requested that China eliminate him;
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized again that he wished to present the former Yuan imperial seal but, fearing Arugtai might intercept it on the way, asked China to eliminate Arugtai;

sentences.zh: 脫脫不花子在中國，請遣還；

translations.literal: Togtoh Buqa's son was in China, and he requested that he be sent back;
translations.idiomatic: Togtoh Buqa's son was being held in China, and he asked that the boy be returned;

sentences.zh: 部屬多從戰有勞，請加賞賚；

translations.literal: many subordinates had followed in battle with merit, and he requested additional rewards;
translations.idiomatic: many of his followers had fought with distinction and he asked for additional rewards;

sentences.zh: 又瓦剌士馬強，請予軍器。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Oirat warriors and horses were strong, and he requested that military equipment be granted.
translations.idiomatic: He also noted that Oirat warriors and horses were strong and asked for arms and equipment.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「瓦剌驕矣，然不足較。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The Oirats have grown arrogant, yet they are not worth contending with.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The Oirats have grown arrogant, but they are not worth taking seriously.

sentences.zh: 」賚其使而遣之。

translations.literal: " He rewarded their envoys and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: " He rewarded their envoys and dismissed them.

sentences.zh: 明年，馬哈木留敕使不遣，復請以甘肅、寧夏歸附韃靼者多其所親，請給還。

translations.literal: The following year, Mahamu detained the imperial envoy and would not send him back, and again requested that those who had submitted from Gansu and Ningxia to the Tartars and were mostly his kin be returned to him.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Mahamu detained the imperial envoy and refused to release him, and again asked that his kinsmen among those who had submitted to the Tartars from Gansu and Ningxia be returned to him.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，命中官海童切責之。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and ordered the eunuch Haitong to rebuke him sternly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged and ordered the eunuch Haitong to deliver a sharp reprimand.

sentences.zh: 冬，馬哈木等擁兵飲馬河，將入犯，而揚言襲阿魯台。

translations.literal: In winter, Mahamu and others massed troops and watered their horses at the river, intending to invade, while publicly declaring they would attack Arugtai.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Mahamu and his allies massed troops on the river where their horses were watered, preparing to invade while claiming they would strike Arugtai.

sentences.zh: 開平守將以聞，帝詔親征。

translations.literal: The defending general at Kaiping reported it, and the emperor ordered a personal campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The Kaiping garrison commander reported this, and the emperor announced he would lead the campaign in person.

sentences.zh: 明年夏，駐蹕忽蘭忽失溫。

translations.literal: The following summer, he halted at Hulun Hubu Hot.
translations.idiomatic: The following summer he encamped at Hulun Hubu Hot.

sentences.zh: 三部埽境來戰，帝麾安遠侯柳升、武安侯鄭亨等先嘗之，而親率鐵騎馳擊，大破之，斬王子十餘人，部眾數千級。

translations.literal: The three tribes came to battle at the frontier; the emperor directed the Marquis of Anyuan, Liu Sheng, the Marquis of Wu'an, Zheng Heng, and others to test them first, then personally led iron cavalry in a charge, inflicting a great defeat, beheading more than ten princes and several thousand of their followers.
translations.idiomatic: All three tribes came to fight at the border. The emperor sent the Marquis of Anyuan, Liu Sheng, the Marquis of Wu'an, Zheng Heng, and others to probe them first, then personally led his armored cavalry in a charge and routed them, killing more than ten princes and several thousand of their followers.

sentences.zh: 追奔，度兩高山，至土剌河。

translations.literal: Pursuing the fugitives, he crossed two high mountains and reached the Tula River.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued the fleeing enemy across two high mountains as far as the Tula River.

sentences.zh: 馬哈木等脫身遁，乃班師。

translations.literal: Mahamu and others escaped with their lives, and the army then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Mahamu and his colleagues escaped, and the army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 明年春，馬哈木等貢馬謝罪，且還前所留使，詞卑。

translations.literal: The following spring, Mahamu and others presented horses in tribute to apologize for their offense, and also returned the envoy previously detained, their words humble.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring Mahamu and his colleagues sent tribute horses to apologize and returned the envoy they had detained, speaking in the most submissive terms.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「瓦剌故不足較。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The Oirats have never been worth contending with.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The Oirats have never been worth taking seriously.

sentences.zh: 」受其獻，館其使者。

translations.literal: " He accepted their tribute and lodged their envoys.
translations.idiomatic: " He accepted their tribute and entertained their envoys.

sentences.zh: 明年，瓦剌與阿魯台戰，敗走。

translations.literal: The following year, the Oirats fought with Arugtai and were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the Oirats fought Arugtai, were defeated, and fled.

sentences.zh: 未幾，馬哈木死，海童歸言，瓦剌拒命由順寧，順寧死，賢義、安樂皆可撫。

translations.literal: Before long, Mahamu died; Haitong returned and reported that the Oirats' defiance had come from Shunningning; with Shunningning dead, Xianyi and Anle could both be pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Mahamu died. On his return Haitong reported that Oirat defiance had stemmed from the Shunningning faction; with Shunningning gone, the Xianyi and Anle factions could both be won over.

sentences.zh: 帝因復使海童往勞太平、把禿孛羅。

translations.literal: The emperor therefore again sent Haitong to console Taiping and Batu Boluo.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accordingly sent Haitong again to convey condolences and rewards to Taiping and Batu Boluo.

sentences.zh: 十六年春，海童偕瓦剌貢使來。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixteenth year, Haitong came together with Oirat tribute envoys.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the sixteenth year, Haitong arrived with Oirat tribute envoys.

sentences.zh: 馬哈木子脫懽請襲爵，帝封為順寧王。

translations.literal: Mahamu's son Toγan requested to inherit the title; the emperor enfeoffed him as King of Shunningning.
translations.idiomatic: Mahamu's son Toγan petitioned to inherit his father's rank, and the emperor enfeoffed him as King of Shunningning.

sentences.zh: 而海童及都督蘇火耳灰等以彩幣往賜太平、把禿孛羅及弟昂克，別遣使祭故順寧王。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Haitong and the commissioner-in-chief Suhuo'erhui and others went with colored silks to bestow gifts on Taiping, Batu Boluo, and the younger brother Angke, and envoys were separately dispatched to perform sacrifices for the late King of Shunningning.
translations.idiomatic: Haitong and Commissioner-in-Chief Suhuo'erhui and others were sent with colored silks to reward Taiping, Batu Boluo, and the younger brother Angke, while separate envoys were dispatched to perform rites for the late King of Shunningning.

sentences.zh: 自是，瓦剌復奉貢。

translations.literal: From this time the Oirats again presented tribute.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the Oirats resumed regular tribute missions.

sentences.zh: 二十年，瓦剌侵掠哈密，朝廷責之，遣使謝罪。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, the Oirats raided Hami; the court rebuked them, and they sent envoys to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year the Oirats raided Hami. When the court rebuked them, they sent envoys to apologize.

sentences.zh: 二十二年冬，瓦剌部屬賽因打力來降，命為所鎮撫，賜彩幣、襲衣、鞍馬，仍令有司給供具。

translations.literal: In the winter of the twenty-second year, the Oirat subordinate Sayindali came to surrender; he was appointed pacification commissioner of his place, and was granted colored silks, ceremonial robes, saddles and horses, while the relevant offices were also ordered to provide supplies.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the twenty-second year the Oirat follower Sayindali surrendered. He was appointed pacification commissioner of his district and given colored silks, court robes, saddles, and horses, and the civil authorities were ordered to furnish his provisions as well.

sentences.zh: 自後來歸者悉如例。

translations.literal: From then on, all who came to submit were treated according to this precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter every defector who came over was treated the same way.

sentences.zh: 四年，脫懽死，子也先嗣，稱太師淮王。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Toγan died; his son Esen succeeded him and styled himself Grand Preceptor and Prince of Huai.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Toγan died and his son Esen succeeded him, taking the title Grand Preceptor and Prince of Huai.

sentences.zh: 於是北部皆服屬也先，脫脫不花具空名，不復相制。

translations.literal: Thereupon the entire north submitted to Esen; Togtoh Buqa held only an empty title and could no longer restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: The northern tribes then all submitted to Esen. Togtoh Buqa retained only a nominal title and could no longer control him.

sentences.zh: 每入貢，主臣並使，朝廷亦兩敕答之；

translations.literal: Whenever they paid tribute, both ruler and minister sent envoys, and the court also issued two edicts in reply;
translations.idiomatic: On each tribute mission both the nominal ruler and Esen sent envoys, and the court answered with two separate edicts;

sentences.zh: 賜賚甚厚，並及其妻子、部長。

translations.literal: the rewards were very generous, extending to their wives, children, and tribal chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: rewards were lavish and extended to their wives, children, and tribal leaders.

sentences.zh: 故事，瓦使不過五十人。

translations.literal: By precedent, Oirat envoys were not to exceed fifty persons.
translations.idiomatic: By established practice, Oirat missions were limited to fifty men.

sentences.zh: 利朝廷爵賞，歲增至二千餘人。

translations.literal: Taking advantage of court ranks and rewards, their numbers each year increased to more than two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Eager for court titles and rewards, their delegations grew to more than two thousand men a year.

sentences.zh: 屢敕，不奉約。

translations.literal: Repeated edicts were issued, but they did not abide by the agreement.
translations.idiomatic: The court issued repeated orders, but they refused to comply.

sentences.zh: 使往來多行殺掠，又挾他部與俱，邀索中國貴重難得之物。

translations.literal: Their envoys coming and going often committed killings and plunder, and they also brought other tribes along with them, demanding rare and precious goods difficult to obtain in China.
translations.idiomatic: Their envoys often killed and plundered along the route, brought other tribes with them, and demanded rare goods that China could scarcely supply.

sentences.zh: 稍不饜，輒造釁端，所賜財物亦歲增。

translations.literal: If they were slightly unsatisfied, they would immediately create incidents; the goods granted them also increased year by year.
translations.idiomatic: At the slightest disappointment they provoked trouble, and the gifts they received grew larger every year.

sentences.zh: 也先攻破哈密，執王及王母，既而歸之。

translations.literal: Esen attacked and captured Hami, seizing the king and the queen mother, but later returned them.
translations.idiomatic: Esen captured Hami and took the king and queen mother prisoner, then later released them.

sentences.zh: 又結婚沙州、赤斤蒙古諸衛，破兀良哈，脅朝鮮。

translations.literal: He also formed marriage alliances with Shazhou, the Chijin Mongol guards, and other posts, defeated the Wuliangha, and intimidated Korea.
translations.idiomatic: He sealed marriage alliances with Shazhou and the Chijin Mongol guards, defeated the Wuliangha, and menaced Korea.

sentences.zh: 邊將知必大為寇，屢疏聞，止敕戒防禦而已。

translations.literal: Border generals knew he would certainly launch a major invasion and repeatedly memorialized the court, but they received only orders to guard and defend.
translations.idiomatic: Border commanders knew a major raid was coming and sent repeated warnings, but the court merely ordered them to stay on the defensive.

sentences.zh: 十一年冬，也先攻兀良哈，遣使抵大同乞糧，並請見守備太監郭敬。

translations.literal: In the winter of the eleventh year, Esen attacked the Wuliangha and sent envoys to Datong to beg for grain, also requesting to see the defending eunuch-director Guo Jing.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the eleventh year Esen attacked the Wuliangha and sent envoys to Datong to request grain and an audience with the garrison eunuch-director Guo Jing.

sentences.zh: 帝敕敬毋見，毋予糧。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Jing not to receive them and not to give grain.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Guo Jing neither to meet them nor to supply grain.

sentences.zh: 明年，復致書宣府守將楊洪。

translations.literal: The following year, he again sent a letter to the Xuanfu defending general Yang Hong.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he wrote again to the Xuanfu commander Yang Hong.

sentences.zh: 洪以聞，敕洪禮其使，報之。

translations.literal: Hong reported it; the emperor ordered Hong to treat their envoys with courtesy and reply.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hong reported this, and the emperor instructed him to receive the envoys courteously and send a reply.

sentences.zh: 頃之，其部眾有來歸者，言也先謀入寇，脫脫不花止之，也先不聽，尋約諸番共背中國。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter, some of their tribesmen came to surrender and reported that Esen was plotting to invade; Togtoh Buqa tried to stop him, but Esen would not listen, and soon he made a pact with various tribes to turn against China together.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward defectors reported that Esen was planning an invasion. Togtoh Buqa tried to dissuade him, but Esen refused to listen and soon enlisted other tribes in a joint revolt against China.

sentences.zh: 帝詔問，不報。

translations.literal: The emperor issued an inquiry, but they gave no reply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent inquiries, but they made no response.

sentences.zh: 時朝使至瓦剌，也先等有所請乞，無不許。

translations.literal: At that time when court envoys reached the Oirats, whatever Esen and the others requested was invariably granted.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever court envoys visited the Oirats, Esen and his party obtained whatever they asked for.

sentences.zh: 瓦剌使來，更增至三千人，復虛其數以冒廩餼。

translations.literal: When Oirat envoys came, their numbers further increased to three thousand, and they again inflated their count to fraudulently claim rations.
translations.idiomatic: Oirat missions now numbered three thousand men, and they again inflated their rolls to claim extra rations.

sentences.zh: 禮部按實予之，所請又僅得五之一，也先大愧怒。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites granted supplies according to the actual count, so what they requested amounted to only one-fifth; Esen was greatly shamed and enraged.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites paid only according to the verified head count, so they received barely a fifth of what they demanded. Esen was deeply humiliated and furious.

sentences.zh: 十四年七月，遂誘脅諸番，分道大舉入寇。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fourteenth year, he then coerced various tribes and launched a major invasion by separate routes.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the fourteenth year he coerced the allied tribes into a full-scale invasion on several fronts.

sentences.zh: 脫脫不花以兀良哈寇遼東，阿剌知院寇宣府，圍赤城，又遣別騎寇甘州，也先自寇大同。

translations.literal: Togtoh Buqa led the Wuliangha to raid Liaodong; Alazhizhi raided Xuanfu and besieged Chicheng; separate cavalry were also sent to raid Ganzhou; Esen himself raided Datong.
translations.idiomatic: Togtoh Buqa led the Wuliangha against Liaodong, Alazhizhi struck Xuanfu and besieged Chicheng, a detached force raided Ganzhou, and Esen attacked Datong in person.

sentences.zh: 參將吳浩戰死貓兒莊，羽書踵至。

translations.literal: Assistant General Wu Hao died in battle at Mao'erzhuang; urgent dispatches arrived one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant General Wu Hao was killed at Mao'erzhuang, and urgent reports poured in.

sentences.zh: 太監王振挾帝親征，群臣伏闕爭，不得。

translations.literal: The eunuch Wang Zhen compelled the emperor to lead a personal campaign; the ministers prostrated themselves at the palace gate in protest but could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Wang Zhen pressed the emperor to lead the campaign in person. Ministers knelt at the palace gate in protest but could not stop him.

sentences.zh: 大同守將西寧侯宋瑛、武進伯硃冕、都督石亨等與也先戰陽和，太監郭敬監軍，諸將悉為所制，失律，軍盡覆。

translations.literal: The Datong defenders, the Marquis of Xining Song Ying, the Earl of Wujin Zhu Mian, the commissioner-in-chief Shi Heng, and others fought Esen at Yanghe; the eunuch Guo Jing supervised the army; the generals were all controlled by him, violated discipline, and the army was entirely destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The Datong commanders—the Marquis of Xining Song Ying, the Earl of Wujin Zhu Mian, and Commissioner-in-Chief Shi Heng—fought Esen at Yanghe under the supervision of the eunuch Guo Jing, who kept the generals under his thumb. They lost discipline and the entire force was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 瑛、冕死，敬伏草中免，亨奔還。

translations.literal: Ying and Mian died; Jing lay hidden in the grass and escaped; Heng fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Song Ying and Zhu Mian were killed. Guo Jing hid in the grass and survived; Shi Heng fled back alive.

sentences.zh: 車駕次大同，連日風雨甚，又軍中常夜驚，人恟懼，郭敬密言於振，始旋師。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage halted at Datong; for days the wind and rain were severe, and the army was constantly alarmed at night; the men were fearful and panicked; Guo Jing secretly spoke to Zhen, and only then did they begin to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial train halted at Datong. Days of heavy rain and nightly alarms spread panic through the army. Only after Guo Jing spoke privately to Wang Zhen did they turn back.

sentences.zh: 車駕還次宣府，敵眾襲軍後。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage returned and halted at Xuanfu; the enemy masses struck the rear of the army.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march the train halted at Xuanfu, and enemy forces struck the rear.

sentences.zh: 恭順侯吳克忠拒之，敗歿。

translations.literal: The Marquis of Gongshun, Wu Kezhong, resisted them and was defeated and killed.
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis of Gongshun, Wu Kezhong, tried to hold them off and was killed in defeat.

sentences.zh: 成國公硃勇、永順伯薛綬以四萬人繼往，至鷂兒嶺，伏發，盡陷。

translations.literal: The Duke of Chengguo Zhu Yong and the Earl of Yongshun Xue Sui followed with forty thousand men; when they reached Yao'erling, an ambush was sprung and they were entirely lost.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Chengguo Zhu Yong and the Earl of Yongshun Xue Sui followed with forty thousand men, but at Yao'erling they walked into an ambush and the whole force was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 次日，至土木。

translations.literal: The next day they reached Tumu.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they reached Tumu.

sentences.zh: 諸臣議入保懷來，振顧輜重遽止，也先遂追及。

translations.literal: The ministers proposed entering Huailai for protection; Zhen, concerned for the baggage train, abruptly stopped it; Esen then caught up.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers urged taking shelter in Huailai, but Wang Zhen, anxious about the baggage train, vetoed the move. Esen caught up with them.

sentences.zh: 土木地高，掘井二丈不得水，汲道已為敵據，眾渴，敵騎益增。

translations.literal: Tumu was on high ground; digging a well twenty feet deep yielded no water; the water route was already held by the enemy; the troops were thirsty, and enemy cavalry steadily increased.
translations.idiomatic: Tumu stood on high ground. Wells dug twenty feet deep found no water, and the streams were already in enemy hands. The army was parched while enemy horsemen gathered in ever greater numbers.

sentences.zh: 明日，敵見大軍止不行，偽退，振遽令移營而南。

translations.literal: The next day, seeing the great army halted and not moving, the enemy feigned a retreat; Zhen hastily ordered the camp moved south.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, seeing the main army immobilized, the enemy pretended to withdraw. Wang Zhen immediately ordered a move south.

sentences.zh: 軍方動，也先集騎四面沖之，士卒爭先走，行列大亂。

translations.literal: As the army had just begun to move, Esen massed cavalry and charged from all four sides; soldiers scrambled to flee first, and the ranks fell into great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as the army stirred, Esen massed his cavalry and charged from every side. Soldiers broke ranks and fled, and the formation collapsed.

sentences.zh: 敵跳陣而入，六軍大潰，死傷數十萬。

translations.literal: The enemy leaped into the formations; the six armies were utterly routed, with hundreds of thousands dead and wounded.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy broke into the lines. The entire army was routed, and hundreds of thousands were killed or wounded.

sentences.zh: 英國公張輔，駙馬都尉井源，尚書鄺埜、王佐，侍郎曹鼐、丁鉉等五十餘人死之，振亦死。

translations.literal: The Duke of Ying Zhang Fu, the imperial son-in-law Jing Yuan, the ministers Kuang Ye and Wang Zuo, the vice ministers Cao Tai and Ding Xuan, and more than fifty others died; Zhen also died.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Ying Zhang Fu, the imperial son-in-law Jing Yuan, Ministers Kuang Ye and Wang Zuo, Vice Ministers Cao Tai and Ding Xuan, and more than fifty others were killed, and Wang Zhen died as well.

sentences.zh: 帝蒙塵，中官喜寧從。

translations.literal: The emperor fell into captivity; the eunuch Xining accompanied him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was taken captive, accompanied by the eunuch Xining.

sentences.zh: 也先聞車駕至，錯愕未之信，及見，致禮甚恭，奉帝居其弟伯顏帖木兒營，以先所掠校尉袁彬來侍。

translations.literal: When Esen heard the imperial carriage had arrived, he was startled and did not believe it; when he saw the emperor, he showed extreme courtesy, lodged the emperor in the camp of his younger brother Bayan Temur, and sent the corporal Yuan Bin, previously captured, to attend him.
translations.idiomatic: Esen could scarcely believe the emperor had fallen into his hands. When they met he treated him with great respect, lodged him in his brother Bayan Temur's camp, and sent the corporal Yuan Bin, whom he had captured earlier, to serve him.

sentences.zh: 也先將謀逆，會大雷雨震死也先所乘馬，復見帝寢幄有異瑞，乃止。

translations.literal: Esen was about to plot treason, but a great thunderstorm struck and killed the horse Esen was riding; he also saw an extraordinary omen at the emperor's sleeping quarters, and therefore stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Esen was plotting treason when a thunderstorm killed his horse and he saw an ominous sign over the emperor's tent. He abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 也先擁帝至大同城，索金幣，都督郭登與白金三萬。

translations.literal: Esen brought the emperor to Datong city and demanded gold and coins; the commissioner-in-chief Guo Deng gave thirty thousand taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: Esen brought the emperor to Datong and demanded gold and silver. Commissioner-in-Chief Guo Deng paid thirty thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 登復謀奪駕入城，帝沮之不果，也先遂擁帝北行。

translations.literal: Deng again plotted to seize the imperial carriage and bring it into the city; the emperor discouraged him and it did not succeed; Esen then brought the emperor north.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Deng then planned to seize the emperor and bring him inside the walls, but the emperor forbade it and the attempt failed. Esen marched the emperor north.

sentences.zh: 九月，郕王自監國即皇帝位，尊帝為太上皇帝。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, the Prince of Cheng, who had been regent, took the throne and honored the emperor as the Retired Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the Prince of Cheng, who had been serving as regent, ascended the throne and honored the captive emperor as the Retired Emperor.

sentences.zh: 也先詭稱奉上皇還，由大同、陽和抵紫荊關，攻入之，直前犯京師。

translations.literal: Esen falsely claimed he was escorting the Retired Emperor back, passed through Datong and Yanghe to reach Zijing Pass, broke through it, and advanced straight to threaten the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Esen pretended he was escorting the Retired Emperor home, marched through Datong and Yanghe to Zijing Pass, broke through, and drove on toward the capital.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書于謙督武清伯石亨、都督孫鏜等御之。

translations.literal: The Minister of War Yu Qian directed the Earl of Wuqing Shi Heng, the commissioner-in-chief Sun Tang, and others to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Yu Qian directed the Earl of Wuqing Shi Heng, Commissioner-in-Chief Sun Tang, and others in the defense.

sentences.zh: 也先邀大臣出迎上皇，未果。

translations.literal: Esen invited the ministers to come out and welcome the Retired Emperor, but it did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Esen demanded that ministers come out to welcome the Retired Emperor, but none did.

sentences.zh: 亨等與戰，數敗之。

translations.literal: Heng and others fought them and repeatedly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Heng and his colleagues fought them and defeated them again and again.

sentences.zh: 也先夜走，自良鄉至紫荊，大掠而出。

translations.literal: Esen fled by night, from Liangxiang to Zijing, plundering heavily as he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Esen fled by night from Liangxiang to Zijing Pass, looting heavily as he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 都督楊洪復大破其餘眾於居庸，也先仍以上皇北行。

translations.literal: The commissioner-in-chief Yang Hong again inflicted a great defeat on their remaining forces at Juyong; Esen still brought the Retired Emperor north.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner-in-Chief Yang Hong routed the remaining enemy at Juyong, while Esen continued north with the Retired Emperor.

sentences.zh: 也先夜常於御幄上，遙見赤光奕奕若龍蟠，大驚異。

translations.literal: Esen often at night looked toward the imperial tent and from afar saw a red glow shining brilliantly like a coiled dragon; he was greatly startled.
translations.idiomatic: At night Esen often looked toward the imperial tent and saw from afar a brilliant red glow like a coiled dragon, which filled him with awe.

sentences.zh: 也先又欲以妹進上皇，上皇卻之，益敬服，時時殺羊馬置酒為壽，稽首行君臣禮。

translations.literal: Esen also wished to offer his younger sister to the Retired Emperor; the Retired Emperor declined, and Esen became even more respectful; from time to time he slaughtered sheep and horses and set out wine to wish long life, bowing his head and performing the rites between ruler and minister.
translations.idiomatic: Esen also offered his sister to the Retired Emperor, who refused her. Esen grew still more deferential, regularly slaughtering sheep and horses for banquets in the emperor's honor and bowing in full court ceremony.

sentences.zh: 景泰元年，也先復奉上皇至大同，郭登不納，仍謀欲奪上皇，也先覺之，引去。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Jingtai reign, Esen again brought the Retired Emperor to Datong; Guo Deng would not receive him and still plotted to seize the Retired Emperor; Esen detected this and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingtai, Esen brought the Retired Emperor to Datong again. Guo Deng refused entry and again plotted to rescue him. Esen sensed the trap and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 初，也先有輕中國心，及犯京師，見中國兵強，城池固，始大沮。

translations.literal: At first Esen had a mind to look down on China; when he attacked the capital and saw China's troops were strong and its walls solid, he became greatly discouraged.
translations.idiomatic: At first Esen had underestimated China, but after assaulting the capital and finding its armies strong and its walls solid, he lost heart.

sentences.zh: 會中國已誘誅賊奄喜寧，失其間諜，而脫脫不花、阿剌知院復遣使與朝廷和，皆撤所部歸，也先亦決意息兵。

translations.literal: It happened that China had lured and executed the traitorous eunuch Xining, losing his spy network; Togtoh Buqa and Alazhizhi again sent envoys to make peace with the court, all withdrawing their forces; Esen also resolved to cease fighting.
translations.idiomatic: China had meanwhile lured the traitor Xining to his death and destroyed Esen's intelligence network. Togtoh Buqa and Alazhizhi sent envoys to sue for peace and withdrew their troops, and Esen too decided to end the war.

sentences.zh: 秋，帝遣侍郎李實、少卿羅綺、指揮馬政等齎璽書往諭脫脫不花及也先。

translations.literal: In autumn, the emperor dispatched the vice minister Li Shi, the junior director Luo Qi, the commander Ma Zheng, and others bearing imperial letters to instruct Togtoh Buqa and Esen.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the emperor sent Vice Minister Li Shi, Junior Director Luo Qi, Commander Ma Zheng, and others with imperial letters to Togtoh Buqa and Esen.

sentences.zh: 而脫脫不花、也先所遣皮兒馬黑麻等已至，帝因復使都御史楊善、侍郎趙榮率指揮、千戶等往。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the envoys sent by Togtoh Buqa and Esen, Pi'ermaheima and others, had already arrived; the emperor therefore again sent the censor-in-chief Yang Shan, the vice minister Zhao Rong, leading commanders, chiliarchs, and others to go.
translations.idiomatic: By then Togtoh Buqa and Esen's envoys, including Pi'ermaheima, had already arrived, so the emperor sent Censor-in-Chief Yang Shan, Vice Minister Zhao Rong, and a party of commanders and chiliarchs in reply.

sentences.zh: 也先語實，兩國利速和，迎使夕至，大駕朝發，但當遣一二大臣來。

translations.literal: Esen told Shi that both states would benefit from a swift peace; if the welcoming envoys arrived in the evening, the imperial carriage could depart at dawn, but only one or two ministers need be sent.
translations.idiomatic: Esen told Li Shi that both sides would gain from a quick peace: if welcoming envoys arrived by evening, the emperor could leave at dawn, and China need send only one or two senior ministers.

sentences.zh: 實歸，善等至，致奉迎上皇意。

translations.literal: Shi returned; Shan and others arrived and conveyed the intention to welcome the Retired Emperor back.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Shi returned, Yang Shan and his party arrived and stated China's wish to bring the Retired Emperor home.

sentences.zh: 也先曰：「上皇歸，當仍作天子邪？

translations.literal: Esen said: "When the Retired Emperor returns, should he again become Son of Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Esen asked, "When the Retired Emperor returns, will he become emperor again?

sentences.zh: 」善曰：「天位已定，不再更。

translations.literal: " Shan said: "The Mandate is already settled and will not be changed again.
translations.idiomatic: " Yang Shan replied, "The throne is already settled and will not change.

sentences.zh: 」也先引善見上皇，遂設宴餞上皇行。

translations.literal: " Esen led Shan to see the Retired Emperor, then held a banquet to send the Retired Emperor on his way.
translations.idiomatic: " Esen then brought Yang Shan to the Retired Emperor and held a farewell banquet.

sentences.zh: 也先席地彈琵琶，妻妾奉酒，顧善曰：「都御史坐。

translations.literal: Esen sat on the ground playing the pipa; his wives and concubines offered wine, and turning to Shan he said: "Censor-in-Chief, be seated.
translations.idiomatic: Esen sat on the ground playing the pipa while his wives served wine. Turning to Yang Shan he said, "Censor-in-Chief, take a seat.

sentences.zh: 」善不敢坐，上皇曰：「太師著坐，便坐。

translations.literal: " Shan dared not sit; the Retired Emperor said: "When the Grand Preceptor tells you to sit, then sit.
translations.idiomatic: " Yang Shan hesitated. The Retired Emperor said, "When the Grand Preceptor bids you sit, sit.

sentences.zh: 」善承旨坐，即起，周旋其間。

translations.literal: " Shan obeyed and sat, then immediately rose and moved about among them.
translations.idiomatic: " He obeyed and sat briefly, then rose again to attend to the company.

sentences.zh: 也先顧善曰：「有禮。

translations.literal: " Esen looked at Shan and said: "Proper manners.
translations.idiomatic: " Esen remarked to him, "You have proper manners.

sentences.zh: 」伯顏等亦各設餞畢，也先築土台，坐上皇台上，率妻妾部長羅拜其下，各獻器用、飲食物。

translations.literal: " Bayan and the others also each held farewell feasts; Esen built an earthen platform, seated the Retired Emperor upon it, and led his wives, concubines, and tribal chiefs in prostration below, each presenting utensils, food, and drink.
translations.idiomatic: " Bayan and the others held their own farewell feasts. Esen built an earthen platform, seated the Retired Emperor on it, and led his wives and tribal chiefs in prostration below, each presenting gifts of vessels, food, and drink.

sentences.zh: 上皇行，也先與部眾皆送約半日程，也先、伯顏乃下馬伏地慟哭曰：「皇帝行矣，何時復得相見！

translations.literal: As the Retired Emperor departed, Esen and his followers all escorted him for about half a day's journey; Esen and Bayan then dismounted, prostrated themselves on the ground, and wept bitterly, saying: "The emperor is leaving—when shall we meet again!
translations.idiomatic: As the Retired Emperor set out, Esen and his followers escorted him for half a day's march. Esen and Bayan then dismounted, prostrated themselves, and wept, crying, "The emperor is leaving—when shall we see him again!

sentences.zh: 」良久乃去，仍遣其頭目七十人送至京。

translations.literal: " After a long while they departed, and still sent seventy of their chiefs to escort him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: " After a long while they took their leave and sent seventy chiefs to escort him all the way to the capital.

sentences.zh: 上皇歸後，瓦剌歲來貢，上皇所亦別有獻。

translations.literal: After the Retired Emperor returned, the Oirats came annually with tribute, and the Retired Emperor's household also made separate offerings.
translations.idiomatic: After the Retired Emperor's return the Oirats sent tribute every year, and the Retired Emperor's household made separate gifts as well.

sentences.zh: 於是帝意欲絕瓦剌，不復遣使往。

translations.literal: Thereupon the emperor wished to cut off relations with the Oirats and no longer sent envoys there.
translations.idiomatic: The reigning emperor then wished to break off contact with the Oirats and stopped sending envoys.

sentences.zh: 也先以為請，尚書王直、金濂、胡濙等相繼言絕之且起釁。

translations.literal: Esen requested it; the ministers Wang Zhi, Jin Lian, Hu Ying, and others in succession said that cutting them off would only provoke trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Esen petitioned for envoys, but Ministers Wang Zhi, Jin Lian, Hu Ying, and others warned in turn that severing ties would only provoke conflict.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「遣使，有前事，適以滋釁耳。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Sending envoys—there is the precedent of what happened before; it would only increase provocations.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "We have the precedent of what happened before—sending envoys would only breed more trouble.

sentences.zh: 曩瓦剌入寇時，豈無使邪？

translations.literal: When the Oirats invaded before, were there not envoys?
translations.idiomatic: When the Oirats invaded before, did we not still have envoys?

sentences.zh: 」因敕也先曰：「前者使往，小人言語短長，遂致失好。

translations.literal: " He therefore instructed Esen: "When envoys went before, petty men's words caused offense, and good relations were lost.
translations.idiomatic: " He instructed Esen, "When envoys went before, petty men's words caused offense and relations soured.

sentences.zh: 朕今不復遣，而太師請之，甚無益。

translations.literal: I shall not send them again now, and though the Grand Preceptor requests it, it would be of little benefit.
translations.idiomatic: I will not send them again, and though the Grand Preceptor asks for them, it would do little good.

sentences.zh: 」也先與脫脫不花內相猜。

translations.literal: " Esen and Togtoh Buqa were mutually suspicious within.
translations.idiomatic: " Esen and Togtoh Buqa grew mutually suspicious.

sentences.zh: 脫脫不花妻，也先姊也，也先欲立其姊子為太子，不從。

translations.literal: Togtoh Buqa's wife was Esen's elder sister; Esen wished to install his sister's son as heir apparent, but Togtoh Buqa would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Togtoh Buqa's wife was Esen's elder sister. Esen wanted her son made heir, but Togtoh Buqa refused.

sentences.zh: 也先亦疑其通中國，將謀己，遂治兵相攻。

translations.literal: Esen also suspected him of communicating with China and plotting against himself, and therefore mobilized troops to attack each other.
translations.idiomatic: Esen also suspected him of colluding with China and plotting against him, and mobilized for war.

sentences.zh: 脫脫不花敗走，也先追殺之，執其妻子，以其人畜給諸部屬；

translations.literal: Togtoh Buqa was defeated and fled; Esen pursued and killed him, seized his wife and children, and distributed his people and livestock among the subordinate tribes;
translations.idiomatic: Togtoh Buqa was defeated and fled. Esen pursued and killed him, seized his family, and distributed his people and livestock among his followers;

sentences.zh: 遂乘勝迫脅諸蕃，東及建州、兀良哈，西及赤斤蒙古、哈密。

translations.literal: then, riding his victory, he coerced various tribes eastward as far as Jianzhou and the Wuliangha, and westward as far as the Chijin Mongols and Hami.
translations.idiomatic: then pressed his advantage to coerce tribes east to Jianzhou and the Wuliangha and west to the Chijin Mongols and Hami.

sentences.zh: 三年冬，遣使來賀明年正旦，尚書王直等復請答使報之。

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year, they sent envoys to congratulate the coming New Year's Day; Minister Wang Zhi and others again requested that return envoys be sent in reply.
translations.idiomatic: That winter they sent envoys to congratulate the New Year. Minister Wang Zhi and others again asked that return envoys be sent.

sentences.zh: 下兵部議，兵部尚書于謙言：「臣職司馬，知戰而已，行人事非所敢聞。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the Ministry of War for discussion; the Minister of War Yu Qian said: "Your servant's duty is to manage horses and knows only warfare; diplomatic matters are not what I dare hear of.
translations.idiomatic: The matter went to the Ministry of War. Minister Yu Qian said, "My duty is military affairs and warfare alone; diplomacy is not for me to decide.

sentences.zh: 」詔仍毋遣使。

translations.literal: " An edict still ordered that no envoys be sent.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict again forbade sending envoys.

sentences.zh: 明年冬，也先自立為可汗，以其次子為太師，來朝，書稱大元田盛大可汗，末曰添元元年。

translations.literal: The following winter, Esen declared himself khan, appointed his second son Grand Preceptor, came to court, and in his letter styled himself Great Yuan Tiansheng Great Khan, ending with the first year of Tianyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The following winter Esen declared himself khan, named his second son Grand Preceptor, and came to court with a letter styling himself Great Yuan Tiansheng Great Khan and dating it the first year of Tianyuan.

sentences.zh: 田盛，猶言天聖也。

translations.literal: Tiansheng means, as it were, "Heaven's Sagacity."
translations.idiomatic: Tiansheng means "Heaven's Sagacity."

sentences.zh: 報書稱曰瓦剌可汗。

translations.literal: The reply letter addressed him as Oirat Khan.
translations.idiomatic: China's reply addressed him only as Oirat Khan.

sentences.zh: 未幾，也先復逼徙朵顏所部於黃河母納地。

translations.literal: Before long, Esen again forced the relocation of the Doyan tribes to the Huanghe Muna region.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Esen again forced the Doyan tribes to move to the Huanghe Muna region.

sentences.zh: 也先恃強，日益驕，荒於酒色。

translations.literal: Relying on his strength, Esen grew daily more arrogant and dissipated himself in wine and women.
translations.idiomatic: Bloated with power, Esen grew ever more arrogant and abandoned himself to wine and women.

sentences.zh: 六年，阿剌知院攻也先，發之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Alazhizhi attacked Esen and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Alazhizhi attacked and killed Esen.

sentences.zh: 韃靼部孛來復殺阿剌，奪也先母妻並其玉璽。

translations.literal: The Tartar chieftain Bolai then killed Ala, seized Esen's mother and wives, and took his jade seal.
translations.idiomatic: The Tartar leader Bolai then killed Ala and seized Esen's mother, wives, and jade seal.

sentences.zh: 也先諸子火兒忽答等徙居干趕河，弟伯都王、侄兀忽納等往依哈密。

translations.literal: Esen's sons Huo'erhuda and others moved to the Ganggan River; his younger brother the Prince of Bodu and his nephew Wuhuna and others went to rely on Hami.
translations.idiomatic: Esen's sons Huo'erhuda and others moved to the Ganggan River, while his brother the Prince of Bodu and his nephew Wuhuna sought refuge in Hami.

sentences.zh: 伯都王，哈密王母之弟也。

translations.literal: The Prince of Bodu was the younger brother of the Hami queen mother.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Bodu was the younger brother of Hami's queen mother.

sentences.zh: 英宗復辟三年，哈密為請封，詔授伯都王都督僉事，兀忽納指揮僉事。

translations.literal: In the third year after the Yingzong Emperor's restoration, Hami petitioned for their enfeoffment; an edict appointed the Prince of Bodu vice commissioner-in-chief and Wuhuna vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year after Emperor Yingzong's restoration, Hami petitioned for their titles. The Prince of Bodu was appointed vice commissioner-in-chief and Wuhuna vice commander.

sentences.zh: 自也先死，瓦剌衰，部屬分散，其承襲代次不可考。

translations.literal: From Esen's death the Oirats declined, their followers scattered, and their succession line cannot be traced.
translations.idiomatic: After Esen's death the Oirats declined, their followers scattered, and their line of succession can no longer be traced.

sentences.zh: 天順中，瓦剌阿失帖木兒屢遣使入貢，朝廷以其為也先孫，循例厚賚之。

translations.literal: During the Tianshun reign, the Oirat Ashi Temur repeatedly sent envoys with tribute; the court, taking him for Esen's grandson, rewarded him generously according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianshun the Oirat Ashi Temur sent tribute repeatedly. The court treated him as Esen's grandson and rewarded him generously by precedent.

sentences.zh: 又撦力克者，常與孛來仇殺。

translations.literal: There was also Chalike, who constantly feuded and fought with Bolai.
translations.idiomatic: Another leader, Chalike, was constantly at war with Bolai.

sentences.zh: 又拜亦撒哈者，常偕哈密來朝。

translations.literal: There was also Baiyisaha, who often came to court together with Hami.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyisaha often came to court together with Hami.

sentences.zh: 其長曰克舍，頗強，數糾韃靼小王子入寇。

translations.literal: Their chief was called Keshe, quite powerful, who several times rallied the Tartar minor princes to invade.
translations.idiomatic: Their chief Keshe was powerful and repeatedly rallied Tartar minor princes for raids.

sentences.zh: 克捨死，養罕王稱雄，擁精兵數萬，克舍弟阿沙為太師。

translations.literal: When Keshe died, the Yanghan King dominated, holding tens of thousands of elite troops; Keshe's younger brother Asha served as Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: After Keshe's death the Yanghan King dominated with tens of thousands of elite troops, while Keshe's brother Asha served as Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 成化二十三年，養罕王謀犯邊，哈密罕慎來告。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Chenghua, the Yanghan King plotted to invade the border; the Hami ruler Shen came to report it.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year of Chenghua the Yanghan King plotted a border raid, and the Hami ruler Shen reported it.

sentences.zh: 養罕不利去，憾哈密，兵還掠其大土剌。

translations.literal: The Yanghan King withdrew without success, resented Hami, and on his return raided its great Tula.
translations.idiomatic: The Yanghan King withdrew without success, bore a grudge against Hami, and on his way back raided its chief city.

sentences.zh: 弘治初，瓦剌中稱太師者，一曰火兒忽力，一曰火兒古倒溫，皆遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the early Hongzhi reign, among the Oirats those styled Grand Preceptor were Huo'erhuli and Huo'ergudaowen, both of whom sent envoys to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Hongzhi two Oirat leaders styled Grand Preceptor—Huo'erhuli and Huo'ergudaowen—both sent tribute missions.

sentences.zh: 土魯番據哈密，都御史許進以金帛厚啖二部，令以兵擊走之。

translations.literal: Turpan occupied Hami; the censor-in-chief Xu Jin lavishly fed the two Oirat factions with gold and silks and ordered them to drive Turpan out with troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Turpan seized Hami, Censor-in-Chief Xu Jin lavished gold and silks on the two Oirat factions and ordered them to drive Turpan out.

sentences.zh: 其部長卜六王者，屯駐把思闊。

translations.literal: Their tribal chief, the King of Boliu, was encamped at Basikuo.
translations.idiomatic: Their chief, the King of Boliu, was encamped at Basikuo.

sentences.zh: 正德十三年，土魯番犯肅州。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Zhengde, Turpan invaded Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Zhengde Turpan invaded Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 守臣陳九疇因遺卜六王彩幣，使乘虛襲破土魯番三城，殺擄以萬計。

translations.literal: The defending official Chen Jiuchou therefore sent colored silks to the King of Boliu, ordering him to seize the opportunity to strike and capture three Turpan cities, killing and capturing by the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison commander Chen Jiuchou sent colored silks to the King of Boliu and ordered him to strike while Turpan was exposed. He captured three cities and killed or captured tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 土魯番畏逼，與之和。

translations.literal: Turpan, fearing pressure, made peace with them.
translations.idiomatic: Turpan, intimidated, made peace with them.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖九年，復以議婚相仇隙。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Jiajing, they again became enemies over marriage negotiations.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Jiajing they fell out again over a marriage dispute.

sentences.zh: 土魯番益強，瓦剌數困敗，又所部輒自殘，多歸中國，哈密復乘間侵掠。

translations.literal: Turpan grew stronger; the Oirats were repeatedly defeated and distressed, and their followers often fought among themselves; many submitted to China; Hami again seized opportunities to raid them.
translations.idiomatic: Turpan grew stronger while the Oirats suffered repeated defeats. Their followers fought among themselves, many defected to China, and Hami again raided them whenever it could.

sentences.zh: 卜六王不支，亦求內附。

translations.literal: The King of Boliu could not hold out and also requested to submit inward.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to hold his ground, the King of Boliu also asked to submit to China.

sentences.zh: 朝廷不許，遣出關，不知所終。

translations.literal: The court did not permit it and sent him out of the passes; his end is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: The court refused and sent him beyond the passes. His fate is unknown.

sentences.zh: 兀良哈三衛

translations.literal: The Three Guards of the Wuliangha
translations.idiomatic: The Three Wuliangha Guards

sentences.zh: 朵顏、福余、泰寧，高皇帝所置三衛也。

translations.literal: Doyan, Fuyu, and Taining were the three guards established by the Gaozu Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Doyan, Fuyu, and Taining were the three guards established by the founding emperor.

sentences.zh: 其地為兀良哈，在黑龍江南，漁陽塞北。

translations.literal: Their territory was Wuliangha, south of the Amur and north of the Yuyang frontier pass.
translations.idiomatic: Their territory was Wuliangha, south of the Amur and north of the Yuyang frontier.

sentences.zh: 漢鮮卑、唐吐谷渾、宋契丹，皆其地也。

translations.literal: In Han it was Xianbei territory; in Tang, Tuyuhun; in Song, Khitan—all the same land.
translations.idiomatic: In Han times it had been Xianbei land; in Tang, Tuyuhun; in Song, Khitan—the same region under different names.

sentences.zh: 元為大寧路北境。

translations.literal: Under the Yuan it was the northern border of Daning Route.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Yuan it formed the northern border of Daning Route.

sentences.zh: 高皇帝有天下，東蕃遼王、惠寧王、朵顏元帥府相率乞內附。

translations.literal: When the Gaozu Emperor gained the realm, the eastern tribes—the Prince of Liao, the Prince of Huining, and the Doyan marshal's office—successively begged to submit.
translations.idiomatic: When the founding emperor took the realm, the eastern tribes—the Prince of Liao, the Prince of Huining, and the Doyan marshal's office—successively submitted.

sentences.zh: 遂即古會州地，置大寧都司營州諸衛，封子權為寧王使鎮焉。

translations.literal: He then took the ancient Huizhou territory, established the Daning regional command and the Yingzhou guards, and enfeoffed his son Quan as Prince of Ning to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: He took the old Huizhou territory, established the Daning command and Yingzhou guards, and enfeoffed his son Quan as Prince of Ning to garrison it.

sentences.zh: 已，數為韃靼所抄。

translations.literal: Before long it was repeatedly raided by the Tartars.
translations.idiomatic: Before long it was repeatedly raided by the Tartars.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十二年置泰寧、朵顏、福余三衛指揮使司，俾其頭目各自領其眾，以為聲援。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Hongwu the three guard commanderies of Taining, Doyan, and Fuyu were established, allowing their chiefs each to lead their own followers as supporting forces.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year of Hongwu the three guard commanderies of Taining, Doyan, and Fuyu were established, each chief leading his own followers as a supporting force.

sentences.zh: 自大寧前抵喜峰口，近宣府，曰朵顏；

translations.literal: From before Daning reaching Xifeng Pass, near Xuanfu, was called Doyan;
translations.idiomatic: From Daning forward to Xifeng Pass, near Xuanfu, was Doyan;

sentences.zh: 自錦、義歷廣寧至遼河，曰泰寧；

translations.literal: from Jin and Yi through Guangning to the Liao River was called Taining;
translations.idiomatic: from Jin and Yi through Guangning to the Liao River was Taining;

sentences.zh: 自黃泥窪逾瀋陽、鐵嶺至開原，曰福余。

translations.literal: from Huangniwa across Shenyang and Tieling to Kaiyuan was called Fuyu.
translations.idiomatic: from Huangniwa across Shenyang and Tieling to Kaiyuan was Fuyu.

sentences.zh: 獨朵顏地險而強。

translations.literal: Doyan alone had rugged terrain and was strong.
translations.idiomatic: Doyan alone occupied rugged terrain and was the strongest.

sentences.zh: 久之皆叛去。

translations.literal: Before long they all rebelled and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long they all rebelled and broke away.

sentences.zh: 成祖從燕起靖難，患寧王躡其後，自永平攻大寧，入之。

translations.literal: The Chengzu Emperor rose from Yan in the Jingnan campaign, fearing the Prince of Ning would follow in his rear; he attacked Daning from Yongping and entered it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chengzu Emperor launched the Jingnan campaign from Yan, he feared the Prince of Ning might strike from behind. He attacked Daning from Yongping and took it.

sentences.zh: 謀脅寧王，因厚賂三衛說之來。

translations.literal: He plotted to coerce the Prince of Ning and therefore lavishly bribed the three guards to persuade them to come.
translations.idiomatic: He plotted to seize the Prince of Ning and lavishly bribed the three guards to join him.

sentences.zh: 成祖行，寧王餞諸郊，三衛從，一呼皆起，遂擁寧王西入關。

translations.literal: As the Chengzu Emperor departed, the Prince of Ning saw him off in the suburbs; the three guards followed, and at one call all rose up, then escorted the Prince of Ning west through the passes.
translations.idiomatic: As the Chengzu Emperor departed, the Prince of Ning saw him off outside the city. The three guards followed, and at a single call they all rose, seized the Prince of Ning, and marched him west through the passes.

sentences.zh: 成祖復選其三千人為奇兵，從戰。

translations.literal: The Chengzu Emperor again selected three thousand of their men as strike troops to follow in battle.
translations.idiomatic: The Chengzu Emperor also selected three thousand of their men as shock troops for the campaign.

sentences.zh: 天下既定，徙寧王南昌，徙行都司於保定，遂盡割大寧地畀三衛，以償前勞。

translations.literal: When the realm was settled, the Prince of Ning was moved to Nanchang, the regional capital was moved to Baoding, and the entire Daning territory was ceded to the three guards to repay their earlier service.
translations.idiomatic: After the realm was settled, the Prince of Ning was moved to Nanchang, the regional capital to Baoding, and all of Daning was given to the three guards as reward for their service.

sentences.zh: 四年冬，三衛飢，請以馬易米。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fourth year, the three guards were starving and requested to exchange horses for grain.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fourth year the three guards were starving and asked to trade horses for grain.

sentences.zh: 帝命有司第其馬之高下，各倍價給之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the officials to grade their horses by quality and pay double the price for each.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered officials to grade their horses and pay double the market price.

sentences.zh: 久之，陰附韃靼掠邊戍，復假市馬來窺伺。

translations.literal: Before long they secretly attached themselves to the Tartars to raid border garrisons, and again used horse markets as cover for reconnaissance.
translations.idiomatic: Before long they secretly joined the Tartars in raiding border posts and used horse markets as cover for spying.

sentences.zh: 帝下詔切責，令其以馬贖罪。

translations.literal: The emperor issued an edict sternly rebuking them and ordered them to atone with horses.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked them sharply and ordered them to atone with horses.

sentences.zh: 十二年春，納馬三千於遼東，帝敕守將王真，一馬各予布四匹。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twelfth year they presented three thousand horses in Liaodong; the emperor instructed the defending general Wang Zhen to give four bolts of cloth for each horse.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the twelfth year they delivered three thousand horses in Liaodong. The emperor instructed the garrison commander Wang Zhen to pay four bolts of cloth per horse.

sentences.zh: 已，復叛附阿魯台。

translations.literal: Before long they rebelled again and attached themselves to Arugtai.
translations.idiomatic: Before long they rebelled again and joined Arugtai.

sentences.zh: 二十年，帝親征阿魯台還，擊之，大敗其眾於屈烈河，斬馘無算，來降者釋勿殺。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, as the emperor returned from a personal campaign against Arugtai, he struck them and inflicted a great defeat on their masses at the Qulie River, beheading and killing beyond count; those who came to surrender were spared.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, returning from a personal campaign against Arugtai, he struck the three guards and routed them at the Qulie River with countless casualties. Those who surrendered were spared.

sentences.zh: 宣宗初，三衛掠永平、山海間，帝將親討之，三衛頭目皆謝罪入貢，撫納之如初。

translations.literal: In the early Xuande reign, the three guards raided between Yongping and Shanhai; the emperor was about to campaign against them in person when their chiefs all apologized and came with tribute, and they were pacified and received as before.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xuande the three guards raided between Yongping and Shanhai. When the emperor prepared to campaign in person, their chiefs all apologized and sent tribute, and they were received as before.

sentences.zh: 七年更給泰寧衛印。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the seal of the Taining Guard was reissued.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the Taining Guard seal was reissued.

sentences.zh: 秋，以朵顏頭目哈剌哈孫、福余頭目安出、泰寧頭目脫火赤等恭事朝廷久，加賜織金彩幣表裡有差。

translations.literal: In autumn, because the Doyan chief Halahasun, the Fuyu chief Anchu, the Taining chief Tuohuochi, and others had long served the court respectfully, additional gifts of brocaded silks, inner and outer garments, were granted in varying amounts.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, because the Doyan chief Halahasun, the Fuyu chief Anchu, the Taining chief Tuohuochi, and others had long been loyal, they received additional brocaded silks and garments in varying quantities.

sentences.zh: 正統間，屢寇遼東、大同、延安境。

translations.literal: During the Zhengtong reign they repeatedly raided the borders of Liaodong, Datong, and Yan'an.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhengtong they repeatedly raided Liaodong, Datong, and Yan'an.

sentences.zh: 獨石守備楊洪擊敗之，擒其頭目朵欒帖木兒。

translations.literal: The Dushi garrison commander Yang Hong defeated them and captured their chief Duoluan Temur.
translations.idiomatic: The Dushi garrison commander Yang Hong defeated them and captured their chief Duoluan Temur.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復附瓦剌也先，泰寧拙赤妻也先以女，皆陰為之耳目。

translations.literal: Before long they again attached themselves to the Oirat Esen; Taining's Zhuochi married Esen's daughter, and all secretly served as his eyes and ears.
translations.idiomatic: Before long they again joined the Oirat Esen. Taining's Zhuochi married Esen's daughter, and all served secretly as his spies.

sentences.zh: 入貢輒易名，且互用其印，又東合建州兵入廣寧前屯。

translations.literal: Whenever they came to tribute they changed their names and even used one another's seals interchangeably; they also joined eastern Jianzhou forces to enter Guangning and Qiantun.
translations.idiomatic: On tribute missions they changed names and even used one another's seals. They also joined Jianzhou forces to raid Guangning and Qiantun.

sentences.zh: 帝惡其反覆，九年春，命成國公硃勇偕恭順侯吳克忠出喜峰，興安伯徐亨出界嶺，都督馬亮出劉家口，都督陳懷出古北，各將精兵萬人，分剿之。

translations.literal: The emperor detested their vacillation; in the spring of the ninth year he ordered the Duke of Chengguo Zhu Yong together with the Marquis of Gongshun Wu Kezhong out from Xifeng, the Earl of Xing'an Xu Heng out from Jieling, Commissioner-in-Chief Ma Liang out from Liujiakou, and Commissioner-in-Chief Chen Huai out from Gubei, each leading ten thousand elite troops to suppress them separately.
translations.idiomatic: Disgusted by their treachery, in the spring of the ninth year the emperor sent the Duke of Chengguo Zhu Yong with the Marquis of Gongshun Wu Kezhong through Xifeng, the Earl of Xing'an Xu Heng through Jieling, Commissioner-in-Chief Ma Liang through Liujiakou, and Commissioner-in-Chief Chen Huai through Gubei—each with ten thousand elite troops—to attack them on separate fronts.

sentences.zh: 勇等捕其擾邊者致闕下，並奪回所掠人畜。

translations.literal: Yong and the others captured those who had disturbed the border and brought them to court, and also recovered the people and livestock they had seized.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yong and his colleagues captured the raiders and brought them to court, recovering the people and livestock they had seized.

sentences.zh: 拙赤等拘肥河衛使人殺之，肥河衛頭目別裡格與戰於格魯坤迭連，拙赤大敗。

translations.literal: Zhuochi and others detained an envoy of the Feihe Guard and killed him; the Feihe chief Bielige fought Zhuochi at Gelukundielian, and Zhuochi was greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuochi detained and killed an envoy of the Feihe Guard. The Feihe chief Bielige fought him at Gelukundielian and routed him.

sentences.zh: 瓦剌復分道截殺，建州亦出兵攻之，三衛大困。

translations.literal: The Oirats again intercepted and killed them on separate routes; Jianzhou also sent troops to attack them; the three guards were greatly distressed.
translations.idiomatic: The Oirats ambushed them on several routes, Jianzhou attacked as well, and the three guards were driven to desperation.

sentences.zh: 十二年春，總兵曹義、參將胡源、都督焦禮等分巡東邊，值三衛入寇，擊之，斬三十二級，擒七十餘人。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twelfth year, the regional commander Cao Yi, the assistant general Hu Yuan, the commissioner-in-chief Jiao Li, and others patrolled the eastern border separately; when the three guards invaded, they struck them, beheading thirty-two and capturing more than seventy.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the twelfth year Regional Commander Cao Yi, Assistant General Hu Yuan, Commissioner-in-Chief Jiao Li, and others patrolled the eastern border. When the three guards invaded, they struck back, killing thirty-two and capturing more than seventy.

sentences.zh: 其年，瓦剌賽刊王復擊殺朵顏乃兒不花，大掠以去。

translations.literal: That year, the Oirat Saikan King again attacked and killed the Doyan chief Nair Buhua and departed after great plunder.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Oirat Saikan King attacked and killed the Doyan chief Nair Buhua and withdrew after heavy looting.

sentences.zh: 也先繼至，朵顏、泰寧皆不支，乞降，福余獨走避腦溫江，三衛益衰。

translations.literal: Esen followed; Doyan and Taining could not hold out and begged to surrender; Fuyu alone fled to avoid the Naowen River; the three guards declined further.
translations.idiomatic: Esen followed. Doyan and Taining could not hold out and surrendered. Fuyu alone fled beyond the Naowen River. The three guards grew weaker still.

sentences.zh: 畏瓦剌強，不敢背，仍歲來致貢，止以利中國賜賚；

translations.literal: Fearing the Oirats' strength, they dared not turn away, and still came annually with tribute, seeking only profit from China's rewards;
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the Oirats, they dared not break away and still sent tribute each year, motivated chiefly by China's rewards;

sentences.zh: 又心銜邊將剿殺，故常潛圖報復。

translations.literal: yet they also harbored resentment at border generals' punitive killings and therefore often secretly plotted revenge.
translations.idiomatic: yet they also resented the border generals' punitive campaigns and often plotted revenge in secret.

sentences.zh: 十四年夏，大同參將石亨等復擊其盜邊者於箭溪山，擒斬五十人，三衛益怨。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fourteenth year, the Datong assistant general Shi Heng and others again struck their border raiders at Jianxishan, capturing and beheading fifty; the three guards grew still more resentful.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the fourteenth year Datong Assistant General Shi Heng and others struck their raiders at Jianxishan, killing or capturing fifty. The three guards grew still more hostile.

sentences.zh: 秋，導瓦剌大入，英宗遂以是役北狩。

translations.literal: In autumn they guided the Oirats in a major invasion; the Yingzong Emperor thereby went north on campaign in this expedition.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn they guided the Oirats in a major invasion, and Emperor Yingzong was captured on the northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 景泰初，朝廷仍遣使撫諭。

translations.literal: In the early Jingtai reign, the court still sent envoys to console and instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jingtai the court still sent envoys to reassure them.

sentences.zh: 三衛受也先旨，數以非時入貢，多遣使往來伺察中國。

translations.literal: The three guards received Esen's orders and repeatedly sent tribute at improper seasons, dispatching many envoys back and forth to spy on China.
translations.idiomatic: Acting on Esen's orders, the three guards sent tribute at irregular times and dispatched many envoys to spy on China.

sentences.zh: 既而也先虐使之，復逼徙朵顏所部於黃河母納地，三衛皆不堪，遂陰輸瓦剌情於中國，請得近邊屯駐。

translations.literal: Before long Esen abused and drove them, again forcing the relocation of the Doyan tribes to Huanghe Muna; the three guards could not endure it and therefore secretly reported Oirat intelligence to China, requesting permission to encamp near the border.
translations.idiomatic: Esen then mistreated them and again forced the Doyan tribes to move to Huanghe Muna. Unable to endure this, the three guards secretly reported Oirat movements to China and asked to camp near the border.

sentences.zh: 舊制，三衛每歲三貢，其貢使俱從喜峰口驗入，有急報則許進永平。

translations.literal: By old regulation the three guards paid tribute three times a year; their tribute envoys all entered through inspection at Xifeng Pass, and in cases of urgent reports they were permitted to enter Yongping.
translations.idiomatic: By established practice the three guards sent tribute three times a year, entering through Xifeng Pass. In emergencies they were allowed into Yongping.

sentences.zh: 時三衛使有自獨石及萬全右衛來者。

translations.literal: At that time there were three-guard envoys coming from Dushi and Wanquan Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: At that time three-guard envoys were arriving through Dushi and Wanquan Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 邊臣以為言，敕止之。

translations.literal: Border officials reported this, and an edict ordered it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Border officials reported this, and the court ordered it stopped.

sentences.zh: 天順中，嘗乘間掠諸邊，復竊通韃靼孛來，每為之鄉導。

translations.literal: During Tianshun they seized opportunities to raid various borders, again secretly communicating with the Tartar Bolai and often serving as his guides.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianshun they seized opportunities to raid the borders, secretly contacted the Tartar Bolai, and often guided his raids.

sentences.zh: 所遣使與孛來使臣偕見。

translations.literal: The envoys they dispatched were received together with Bolai's envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Their envoys were received together with Bolai's.

sentences.zh: 中國待韃靼厚，請加賞不得，大忿，遂益與孛來相結。

translations.literal: China treated the Tartars generously; their request for additional rewards was denied, and they were greatly enraged, then increasingly allied with Bolai.
translations.idiomatic: China treated the Tartars generously, but their request for extra rewards was denied. Enraged, they drew closer to Bolai.

sentences.zh: 十四年詔復三衛馬市。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year an edict restored the horse markets for the three guards.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year the court restored the three guards' horse markets.

sentences.zh: 初，國家設遼東馬市三，一城東，一廣寧，皆以待三衛。

translations.literal: Initially the state established three Liaodong horse markets—one at Chengdong, one at Guangning—all to serve the three guards.
translations.idiomatic: The state had originally established three Liaodong horse markets—at Chengdong and Guangning among them—all for the three guards.

sentences.zh: 正統間，以其部眾屢叛，罷之。

translations.literal: During Zhengtong, because their followers repeatedly rebelled, the markets were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhengtong their followers rebelled repeatedly, and the markets were closed.

sentences.zh: 會韃靼滿都魯暴強，侵掠三衛，三衛頭目皆走避塞下。

translations.literal: It happened that the Tartar Mandulu grew violent and strong, raiding the three guards; their chiefs all fled to take refuge below the passes.
translations.idiomatic: The Tartar Mandulu grew powerful and raided the three guards until their chiefs all fled to the border passes for refuge.

sentences.zh: 數飢困，請復馬市再四，不許。

translations.literal: Repeatedly starving and distressed, they requested restoration of the horse markets four times, but were not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Repeatedly starving, they petitioned four times to reopen the horse markets but were refused.

sentences.zh: 至是巡撫陳鉞為帝言，始許之。

translations.literal: At this time the grand coordinator Chen Yue spoke to the emperor on their behalf, and permission was finally granted.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Chen Yue then persuaded the emperor, and permission was finally granted.

sentences.zh: 滿都魯死，亦思馬因主兵柄，三衛復數為所窘。

translations.literal: When Mandulu died, Yisimayin held military power, and the three guards were again repeatedly harassed by him.
translations.idiomatic: After Mandulu's death Yisimayin took command of the troops and again repeatedly harassed the three guards.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，韃靼別部那孩擁三萬眾入大寧、金山，涉老河，攻殺三衛頭目伯顏等，掠去人畜以萬計。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, the separate Tartar branch Nahai led thirty thousand men into Daning and Jinshan, crossed the Lao River, attacked and killed the three-guard chiefs Bayan and others, and carried off people and livestock by the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year the Tartar leader Nahai led thirty thousand men into Daning and Jinshan, crossed the Lao River, killed chiefs including Bayan, and carried off tens of thousands of people and livestock.

sentences.zh: 三衛乃相率攜老弱，走匿邊圉。

translations.literal: The three guards then led one another, bringing the old and weak, to flee and hide within the border enclosures.
translations.idiomatic: The three guards then fled en masse with their families to seek refuge inside the border defenses.

sentences.zh: 邊臣劉潺以聞，詔予芻糧優飖之。

translations.literal: The border official Liu Chan reported it; an edict granted them fodder and grain with generous relief.
translations.idiomatic: Border official Liu Chan reported this, and the court granted them fodder and grain with generous relief.

sentences.zh: 弘治初，常盜掠古北、開原境，守臣張玉、總兵李杲等以計誘斬其來市者三百人，遂北結脫羅干，請為復仇，數寇廣寧、寧遠諸處。

translations.literal: In the early Hongzhi reign they often raided the borders of Gubei and Kaiyuan; the defending official Zhang Yu and the regional commander Li Gao and others by stratagem lured and beheaded three hundred of those who came to market, whereupon they allied north with Tuoluo Gan and requested revenge, repeatedly raiding Guangning, Ningyuan, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Hongzhi they often raided Gubei and Kaiyuan. Defending official Zhang Yu and Regional Commander Li Gao lured three hundred men who came to market and executed them. The three guards then allied with Tuoluo Gan to the north and repeatedly raided Guangning and Ningyuan.

sentences.zh: 時海西尚古者，以不得通貢叛中國，數以兵阻諸蕃入貢，諸蕃並銜之。

translations.literal: At that time Shanggu of Haixi, because he could not send tribute, rebelled against China and repeatedly used troops to block various tribes from bringing tribute; all the tribes resented him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Shanggu of Haixi, denied tribute access, rebelled and repeatedly blocked other tribes' missions. All resented him.

sentences.zh: 朝廷旋許尚古納款，撫寧猛克帖木兒等皆以尚古為辭，入寇遼陽，殺掠甚眾。

translations.literal: The court soon permitted Shanggu to submit; Funing, Mengketemur, and others all used Shanggu as their pretext to invade Liaoyang, killing and plundering in great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: The court soon accepted Shanggu's submission, but Funing, Mengketemur, and others used him as a pretext to invade Liaoyang with heavy killing and plunder.

sentences.zh: 韃靼小王子屢掠三衛，三衛因各叩關輸罪，朝廷許之，然陽為恭順而已。

translations.literal: The Tartar minor princes repeatedly raided the three guards; the three guards therefore each came to the passes to confess guilt, and the court permitted it, yet they were only outwardly submissive.
translations.idiomatic: Tartar minor princes repeatedly raided them. The three guards each came to the passes to confess and were forgiven, but their submission was only for show.

sentences.zh: 朵顏都督花當者，恃險而驕，數請增貢加賞，不許。

translations.literal: The Doyan commissioner-in-chief Huadang relied on rugged terrain and was arrogant, repeatedly requesting increased tribute and rewards, which were not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The Doyan commissioner Huadang, relying on rugged terrain, grew arrogant and repeatedly asked for more tribute and rewards, but was refused.

sentences.zh: 正德十年，花當子把兒孫以千騎毀鯰魚關，入馬蘭谷大掠，參將陳乾戰死；

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Zhengde, Huadang's son Ba'ersun with a thousand cavalry destroyed Nianyu Pass, entered Malan Valley for great plunder, and Assistant General Chen Qian died in battle;
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Zhengde Huadang's son Ba'ersun led a thousand horsemen to destroy Nianyu Pass and raid Malan Valley. Assistant General Chen Qian was killed;

sentences.zh: 復以五百騎入板場谷，千騎入神山嶺，又千餘騎入水開洞。

translations.literal: again with five hundred cavalry he entered Banchang Valley, a thousand into Shenshan Ridge, and more than a thousand into Shuikaidong.
translations.idiomatic: he then sent five hundred horsemen into Banchang Valley, a thousand into Shenshan Ridge, and more than a thousand into Shuikaidong.

sentences.zh: 事聞，命副總兵桂勇御之。

translations.literal: When this was reported, the vice regional commander Gui Yong was ordered to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: When this was reported, Vice Regional Commander Gui Yong was ordered to repel them.

sentences.zh: 花當退去，屯駐紅羅山，匿把兒孫，使其子打哈等入朝請罪，詔釋不問。

translations.literal: Huadang withdrew and encamped at Hongluo Mountain, hiding Ba'ersun and sending his son Daha and others to court to beg forgiveness; an edict pardoned them without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Huadang withdrew to Hongluo Mountain, hid Ba'ersun, and sent his son Daha to court to apologize. They were pardoned.

sentences.zh: 十三年，帝巡幸至大喜峰口，將征三衛頭目，使悉詣關下宴勞，不果。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the emperor on tour reached Daxifeng Pass, intending to campaign against the three-guard chiefs and summon them all below the pass for a feast and rewards, but it did not come to pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the emperor on tour reached Daxifeng Pass, planning to summon the three-guard chiefs below the pass for a feast, but the plan failed.

sentences.zh: 當把兒孫犯邊時，朝廷詔削其職。

translations.literal: When Ba'ersun violated the border, the court ordered his rank stripped.
translations.idiomatic: When Ba'ersun raided the border, the court stripped his rank.

sentences.zh: 把兒孫死，其子伯革入貢。

translations.literal: When Ba'ersun died, his son Boge came with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: After Ba'ersun's death his son Boge sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖九年，詔予伯革父爵，而打哈自以花當子不得職，怒，遂先後掠冷口、擦崖、喜峰間。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Jiajing an edict granted Boge his father's rank; Daha, taking himself for Huadang's son and denied office, was angry and then successively raided between Lengkou, Cayai, and Xifeng.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Jiajing Boge was granted his father's rank. Daha, angry that he as Huadang's son received no office, raided Lengkou, Cayai, and Xifeng in succession.

sentences.zh: 參將袁繼勳等失於防禦，皆逮治。

translations.literal: Assistant Generals Yuan Jixun and others failed in defense and were all arrested and punished.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Generals Yuan Jixun and others were arrested for failing in defense.

sentences.zh: 十七年春，指揮徐顥誘殺泰寧部九人，其頭目把當亥率眾寇大清堡，總兵馬永擊斬之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the seventeenth year, Commander Xu Hao lured and killed nine men of the Taining tribe; their chief Badanghai led the masses to raid Daqing Fort; the regional commander Ma Yong struck and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the seventeenth year Commander Xu Hao lured and killed nine Taining tribesmen. Their chief Badanghai raided Daqing Fort and was killed by Regional Commander Ma Yong.

sentences.zh: 其屬把孫以朵顏部眾復入，鎮守少監王永與戰，敗績。

translations.literal: His follower Basun again entered with Doyan tribesmen; the garrison eunuch-director Wang Yong fought them and was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: His follower Basun invaded again with Doyan tribesmen. Garrison eunuch-director Wang Yong fought them and was defeated.

sentences.zh: 二十二年冬，攻圍墓田谷，殺守備陳舜，副總兵王繼祖等赴援，擊斬三十餘級。

translations.literal: In the winter of the twenty-second year they attacked and besieged Mutian Valley, killing the garrison commander Chen Shun; Vice Regional Commander Wang Jizu and others went to relieve them and struck down more than thirty.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the twenty-second year they besieged Mutian Valley and killed Garrison Commander Chen Shun. Vice Regional Commander Wang Jizu relieved the siege and killed more than thirty raiders.

sentences.zh: 其年，詔罷舊設三衛馬市，並新設木市亦罷之。

translations.literal: That year an edict abolished the old-established horse markets of the three guards, and the newly established timber markets were also abolished.
translations.idiomatic: That year the court abolished the three guards' horse markets and the newly established timber markets as well.

sentences.zh: 秋，三衛復導韃靼寇遼州，入沙河堡，守將張景福戰死。

translations.literal: In autumn the three guards again guided the Tartars to raid Liaozhou, entered Shahe Fort, and the defending general Zhang Jingfu died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the three guards again guided Tartar raiders into Liaozhou and Shahe Fort. Defending general Zhang Jingfu was killed.

sentences.zh: 三衛之迭犯也，實朵顏部哈舟兒、陳通事為之。

translations.literal: The repeated violations of the three guards were in fact carried out by the Doyan tribesmen Hazhou'er and Chen Tongshi.
